system_description.narrative_title: Geopolitical shocks rewire global energy supply and market volatility
system_description.narrative_summary: A cluster of geopolitical events — Middle East attacks on energy and transport infrastructure and sudden diplomatic moves over Russia-Ukraine energy supplies — is driving sharp uncertainty in oil, diesel and related markets. That uncertainty propagates through shipping routes, insurance and airline operations, commodity prices, and financial markets, while prompting policy responses from central banks and governments. The system is open: supply-side shocks, strategic deals, and security risks interact with market expectations, creating reinforcing and balancing feedbacks that affect inflation, capital flows, and energy-transition decisions.
system_description.scope: Global crude, diesel and LNG supply chains (production, storage, shipping, refineries), physical chokepoints and transport nodes (airports, tankers, routes), market mechanisms (spot/futures prices, tanker rates, insurers), major state and non-state actors affecting supply (Russia, Gulf states, Iran-backed Houthis), traders and refiners, and financial and policy actors responding (central banks, finance ministers, IMF/World Bank, airlines).
system_description.super_system: The international geopolitical-economic system (global security architecture integrated with the world economy and energy-transition dynamics).
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and monetary policy
Maritime logistics, insurance and freight markets
Regional security architectures (Middle East; Russia–Ukraine/Eastern Europe)

variables.name: Hydrocarbon supply flow
variables.description: Net physical flow rate of crude oil, diesel and LNG delivered into global markets (e.g., barrels or tonnes per day).

variables.name: Spare production capacity
variables.description: Available additional upstream production capacity that can be brought online within a definable short-to-medium timeframe.

variables.name: Refined fuel inventories
variables.description: Aggregate stock of refined petroleum products held in commercial and strategic storage globally.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: Proportion of global refining capacity that is operational and processing feedstock at a given time.

variables.name: Maritime transit delay rate
variables.description: Average voyage time delays for energy shipments across key sea routes relative to baseline transit times.

variables.name: Shipping-route security risk
variables.description: Level of security risk (theft, attack, interdiction, interdiction risk) perceived along maritime and chokepoint routes used for energy transport.

variables.name: Tanker freight rates
variables.description: Market price level for shipping crude and refined products (e.g., $/ton or $/voyage) reflecting transport costs.

variables.name: Insurance premium index
variables.description: Average insurance premium level charged for covering energy cargoes and vessels on relevant routes.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure attack rate
variables.description: Frequency of successful or attempted kinetic or disruptive attacks on production, refining, storage or transport nodes per unit time.

variables.name: Market price volatility
variables.description: Short- to medium-term variability (variance) of wholesale prices for crude oil, diesel and related energy commodities.

variables.name: Market uncertainty perception
variables.description: Degree of collective uncertainty or ambiguity among market participants about future supply, demand and policy conditions.

variables.name: Capital flow volatility
variables.description: Variability in cross-border and sectoral financial flows into and out of energy markets and related assets.

variables.name: Policy response level
variables.description: Magnitude and intensity of monetary, fiscal and regulatory actions directed at energy markets and macroeconomic stabilization.

variables.name: Inflationary pressure
variables.description: Broad upward pressure on consumer and producer prices attributable in part to changes in energy costs and supply disruptions.

variables.name: Energy-transition investment rate
variables.description: Flow of capital deployed into low-carbon energy technologies, infrastructure and related transition activities per unit time.

variables.name: Strategic reserve level
variables.description: Quantity held in strategic petroleum or fuel reserves available for deliberate release to stabilize markets.

catalysts.title: Fraying Russia–Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'
catalysts.description: Reports that the announced Russia‑Ukraine energy ceasefire is breaking down, undermining promised fuel flows and raising market uncertainty.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire'; reports the ceasefire 'frays' and 'collides with real‑world problems.'

catalysts.title: Potential surge in Russian diesel exports
catalysts.description: Russian claims and US statements about a diesel supply deal point to higher Russian diesel volumes entering markets in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump’s diesel‑supply deal with Russia'; 'Russia says its diesel exports may exceed volumes announced.'

catalysts.title: Houthi strikes and Saudi airport disruptions
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi attacks (including Riyadh airport strikes) and related airport shutdowns raise transport risks and disrupt regional energy logistics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthi strike on Saudi airport kills 12'; 'Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week'; 'Attacks on Saudi airports threaten...'.

catalysts.title: Tanker freight squeeze and regional heavy‑oil glut
catalysts.description: Rising attacks and longer voyages are pushing tanker rates up, creating a heavy‑oil glut in the Americas and barrel shortages in Asia/Europe.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil tanker rates surge amid rising attacks, longer voyages'; 'Americas have glut of heavy oil; Asia, Europe scramble for barrels.'

catalysts.title: Panama quakes risk canal disruption
catalysts.description: A series of powerful earthquakes and aftershocks in Panama raises the risk of canal disruption and wider shipping delays for energy cargoes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Panama suffers over 200 aftershocks after Friday's 7.7‑magnitude earthquake'; 'Magnitude 6 earthquake strikes Panama.'

catalysts.title: EU investigates oil & gas windfall tax
catalysts.description: EU consideration of a windfall profits tax on oil and gas could trigger regulatory action, market repricing and capital flow responses in energy sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU looking at oil and gas windfall profit tax, as energy prices soar.'

catalysts.title: EU pushes climate ambition ahead of COP31
catalysts.description: EU efforts to accelerate CO2 cuts at COP31 may spur near‑term policy signaling and shift investment toward low‑carbon projects.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU eyes COP31 climate deal to accelerate CO2 cuts.'

catalysts.title: Saudi‑Iran diplomatic engagement
catalysts.description: Foreign‑minister level talks between Saudi Arabia and Iran could ease regional tensions, lowering transport risks and market uncertainty if sustained.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi, Iranian foreign ministers discuss regional tensions, state news agency says.'

catalysts.title: Escalation in Middle East and Ukraine
catalysts.description: Renewed fighting in the Middle East and strikes in Ukraine are likely to increase attacks on energy assets and raise price volatility and insurance costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil Climbs as Fighting Flares in Middle East, Ukraine'; 'Russian strike on Kyiv...'; 'Oil Futures Extend Gains on Persistent Supply Concerns.'
